scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being a "nass" (which I think is Yiddish for "idiot") in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, my wife and I didn't do a lot of traditional things for our wedding, which is fine. One thing she really wanted was for me not to see her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed to that, and she kept showing me pictures of grooms crying when they see their brides for the first time, tagging me in and saying that would be my reaction. On the day of the wedding, she looked beautiful, as always. But honestly, I didn't think the dress was flattering on her. I tried not to focus on that and just looked at her, smiled, and didn't cry like in those pictures. The maid of honor kept nudging me, mouthing "stop," which was kind of annoying. After the wedding and honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend (the maid of honor) and found out that I didn't react as she expected. She mentioned that there were pictures where I didn't look how she pictured. I told her I didn't want to cry and that it was a big day, but I thought my happiness was clear without being overly dramatic. I also mentioned that the maid of honor was nudging me the whole time, which I felt was unfair. Finally, I asked if we had a wedding or a play because I never got any cues. Now she's mad at me. I feel bad she's disappointed, but I couldn't force myself to have that reaction. So, am I being a nass here? Let me think about this. On one hand, I respected her wish not to see the dress beforehand. I was supportive and agreed to it. On the day, I focused on her, smiled, and participated in the ceremony. I didn't make a big deal about the dress, which might have been a point of contention. But she expected a certain reaction, like crying, based on the pictures she showed me. I didn't deliver that, which made her feel let down. The maid of honor's nudging added to the pressure, making me feel like I wasn't reacting enough. I also pointed out that it felt like a play because I wasn't getting any cues, which might have come off as dismissive or unappreciative of the effort put into the wedding. So, was I being a nass? Maybe in the sense that I didn't meet her expectations, but I also didn't do anything wrong. I was honest about my feelings and reactions. It's a tough spot because weddings are emotional and personal, and everyone has different ways of expressing themselves. I think the key here is communication. Maybe I should have talked to her about my feelings before the wedding, or after, to explain why I didn't react the way she expected. It's important to acknowledge her feelings and make sure she feels valued, even if our expressions of happiness differ.
